title: Field-Closure of Algebraicity via Integral Closure
content: The four closure lemmas (isAlgebraic_add, _neg, _sub, _mul) all follow one template: rewrite every IsAlgebraic hypothesis and the goal with isAlgebraic_iff_isIntegral, then apply the matching integral-closure subring lemma (IsIntegral.add/neg/sub/mul). The inverse lemma isAlgebraic_inv is even shorter — it is exactly Mathlib's IsAlgebraic.inv. The reduction is valid precisely because K is a field, where algebraic and integral coincide.
mathContext: $\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\,K\,x \iff \mathrm{IsIntegral}\,K\,x$ over a field $K$; the integral elements form a subring, so algebraic elements are closed under $+,-,\times$.

title: algebraicSubfield: The Algebraic Numbers as a Subfield
content: Bundles the closure lemmas of §1 into a Subfield L whose carrier is {x | IsAlgebraic K x}. The six subfield obligations are discharged by the closure lemmas plus isAlgebraic_one and isAlgebraic_zero. Instantiated at K = ℚ, L = ℂ this is the field of algebraic numbers; combined with the parent's countability result it is a countable subfield of ℂ. The mem_algebraicSubfield simp lemma exposes membership as plain algebraicity (Iff.rfl).
mathContext: $\mathrm{algebraicSubfield}\,K\,L = \{x \in L \mid \mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\,K\,x\}$, a subfield of $L$; at $K=\mathbb{Q},\,L=\mathbb{C}$ it is $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\cap\mathbb{C}$.

title: The Back-Substitution Contradiction
content: The engine behind every transcendence-preservation theorem. To show t + a is transcendental, assume it is algebraic; then t = (t + a) − a is a difference of two algebraic numbers, algebraic by isAlgebraic_sub, contradicting Transcendental K t. The proof is literally `intro h; exact ht (by simpa using isAlgebraic_sub h ha)`. Every other operation is the same move with a different inverse identity: a⁻¹·(a·t) for products, etc.
mathContext: $t = (t+a) - a$; if $t+a$ and $a$ are algebraic so is $t$ — contradiction. Transcendence is the contrapositive of subfield closure.

title: Nonzero Algebraic Rescaling Preserves Transcendence
content: If a ≠ 0 is algebraic and t transcendental, then a·t is transcendental: were it algebraic, t = a⁻¹·(a·t) would be a product of algebraics (isAlgebraic_inv ha times the assumption), made explicit by simp with inv_mul_cancel_left₀ ha0. The nonzero hypothesis is essential — 0·t = 0 is algebraic. transcendental_mul_algebraic is the mul_comm mirror.
mathContext: $a \ne 0$ algebraic, $t$ transcendental $\implies a\cdot t$ transcendental, since $t = a^{-1}(a\,t)$.

title: Capstone: Algebraic Affine Maps Preserve Transcendence
content: transcendental_affine packages the additive and multiplicative translates into one statement: for a ≠ 0 and a, b algebraic, t ↦ a·t + b sends every transcendental to a transcendental. The proof composes transcendental_algebraic_mul (for a·t) with transcendental_add_algebraic (for +b). This is the form most often invoked in practice — the transcendentals are invariant under every algebraic affine map.
mathContext: $t \mapsto a\,t + b$ with $a \ne 0$, $a,b$ algebraic, maps transcendentals to transcendentals.

title: The Transcendentals Are NOT a Subfield
content: A sharp structural contrast with §1: for any transcendental t, both t and 1−t are transcendental (transcendental_algebraic_sub against isAlgebraic_one), yet their sum t + (1−t) = 1 is algebraic. So the transcendentals are closed under no field operation — they are exactly the set-theoretic complement of the algebraic subfield, and the complement of a nontrivial subfield is never itself a subfield.
mathContext: $t,\,1-t$ transcendental but $t + (1-t) = 1 \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$; the transcendentals are the complement of a subfield.

title: Sanity Checks over ℚ ⊆ ℂ
content: Concrete instantiations at K = ℚ, L = ℂ for an arbitrary transcendental t: t+1, t⁻¹, t², and 1−t are all transcendental, demonstrating the general theorems on the complex numbers. Witnesses exist abundantly (the sibling leaves show uncountably many transcendental reals/complexes); classical examples include e, π, and any Liouville number.
